title: Binance hack: developing story
summary: The largest crypto theft on record: on Oct 29 attackers moved about US$6.3 billion (Binance's estimate) out of Binance's own hot wallets on 10 blockchains. About US$3 billion has been frozen. Binance said on Nov 1 that about 95% of the stolen amount has been replenished from company funds (up from about 90% on Oct 31) and reopened withdrawals on Sunday in stages, Bitcoin first; all 15 first-phase networks were open by 7:36 a.m. ET, with other networks to come after security checks. Binance said net withdrawals were about US$3.64 billion in the first nine and a half hours. On Nov 2 a Binance spokesperson told Reuters net withdrawals since the Sunday restart had reached US$4.72 billion, about 2.8% of assets on the platform, and that withdrawals were slowing; Circle said it had frozen more than US$1.1 billion in USDC. On Nov 1 the FBI formally blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group. On Nov 2 Binance completed a zero-knowledge proof-of-reserves snapshot covering 10 assets, plans another snapshot on Nov 4, and began a second phase reopening withdrawals for more assets on several networks at 04:00 UTC on Tuesday, Nov 3 (The Block; crypto.news; Reuters via Global Banking & Finance; Grafa). DefiLlama data showed net outflows of about US$6.1 billion on Sunday and US$2.57 billion on Monday, and Binance reopened five more fiat currencies, including the US dollar, on Monday (Cointelegraph; Blockonomi). On Nov 3 Binance CEO Richard Teng shared on-chain data showing cumulative net outflows of about US$5.28 billion since the hack and hourly deposits exceeding withdrawals by about US$10 million at 03:00 UTC (CoinDesk).

facts.label: Stolen
facts.note: Binance's own estimate of the impact (Reuters); TRM Labs: about US$6.36B moved out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains; Chainalysis's Jonathan Levin put it at US$6.4B in a later update (Cointelegraph, 05:01 UTC Oct 30)
facts.source: Reuters via Investing.com; Cointelegraph live updates

facts.label: Frozen so far
facts.note: Binance said verified frozen assets reached about US$3B (00:52 UTC Oct 30), including more than US$1.567B USDT frozen by Tether and more than US$800M USDC by Circle; First Digital froze the FDUSD involved; on Nov 2 Circle said it had frozen more than US$1.1B in USDC (Reuters via Business Recorder); Chainalysis counted about US$2.8B frozen as of 11:30 a.m. ET Nov 3, including nearly US$1.57B by Tether and more than US$800M by Circle (FinanceFeeds, Nov 5, citing Chainalysis)

facts.label: Still with the attacker
facts.note: Bitquery's count of the attacker's wallets, mostly ether and bitcoin (06:43 UTC Oct 30; Euronews reported US$3.1B from an earlier count). A different measure, TRM Labs' funds 'beyond the reach of token issuers', was about US$2.4B (00:30 UTC Oct 30). Stolen, frozen and still held come from different sources and times, so they need not add up

facts.label: Recovered
facts.value: about 98% of the affected assets backfilled (Binance, Nov 4); no recovered amount published
facts.note: Binance said on Nov 4 that about 98% of the affected assets have been backfilled, up from about 95% on Nov 1; the remaining 2% are low-liquidity tokens it will keep buying through market and OTC channels, and it says it set aside more than 100% of the required amount from its own funds (PANews; TechFlow). It has not said how much frozen money has come back

facts.label: When
facts.note: most of the money left within about 20 minutes (TRM Labs; Yahoo Finance), and the attacker kept moving funds out of 17 hot wallets until about 7:56 p.m. ET (Bitquery, via Euronews). The first public signs came about an hour after it began: Changpeng Zhao's post at about 5:15 p.m. ET, then Binance's statement

facts.label: Who
facts.value: North Korea's TraderTraitor, a Lazarus-linked unit (FBI, Nov 1)
facts.note: The FBI formally attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group in a public alert on Nov 1, saying it stole more than US$6 billion and is converting the coins mainly into ether (RTE; ABC News Australia; Newsweek; Fox Business). TRM Labs and Chainalysis had reached the same assessment on Oct 30; North Korea routinely denies such attacks

facts.label: Binance
facts.value: deposits working normally; withdrawals restarted in stages from Nov 1 (15 networks in the first phase, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Tron, Solana and XRP Ledger), and a second phase reopening more assets on several networks (including BSC, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, SUI, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base) from 04:00 UTC on Tuesday Nov 3; on Nov 2 it completed a zero-knowledge proof-of-reserves snapshot for 10 assets (BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, ZEC), and on Nov 4 a new snapshot widened coverage to 44 tokens; says it will cover all losses with company funds
facts.note: The Block (11:52 a.m. ET Nov 2) and crypto.news report the 10-asset proof-of-reserves snapshot; co-CEO Yi He said the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to generate after the Nov 4 snapshot; second phase from 04:00 UTC Nov 3, prioritised by the past week's withdrawal demand, each network after security checks (Global Banking & Finance, citing Reuters, Nov 3; Grafa, Nov 3); on Nov 3 CEO Richard Teng posted on-chain data showing about US$5.28B cumulative net outflows and hourly deposits above withdrawals at 03:00 UTC (CoinDesk, 7:57 a.m. ET Nov 3); the Nov 4 snapshot covers 44 tokens and Binance says the full zero-knowledge proof takes 50 to 60 hours to generate (PANews; TechFlow, Nov 4)
